reason: The text explicitly describes the Hebrew people (David's men) complaining about their leader David. When David and his men returned to Ziklag to find their city burned and their families taken captive by the Amalekites, the passage states: 'וַתֵּ֨צֶר לְדָוִ֜ד מְאֹ֗ד כִּֽי־ אָמְר֤וּ הָעָם֙ לְסָקְל֔וֹ' (And it was very distressing for David because the people spoke of stoning him). The people were expressing their grievance and anger toward David, their leader, for what had befallen their families. David had to strengthen himself in the Lord precisely because of this complaint against his leadership.
